proxy.name: documented deterministic proxy (WP2_SPEC); tiktoken o200k_base used only if importable

environment_probe.tiktoken: NOT importable: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tiktoken'
environment_probe.regex: NOT importable: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'regex'

proxy.whole_wire_text_definition: instructions + canonical schema JSON + json.dumps(wire['input']) with the SDK's compact separators; the same definition the supervisor spike used
proxy.known_limitation: one scalar factor cannot fix a per-character-class bias: if the measured tokens-per-proxy-unit of the anchored static prefix differs from that of the volatile evidence body, a single global factor systematically mis-weights one of them.  calibration.json's static_factor vs dynamic_factor columns measure exactly that spread; per-subtree tokens are emitted under both regimes.

calibrated_error_pct.definition: the per-request factor is exact on its own request by construction, so the reported calibrated error is leave-one-out: the factor learned from every OTHER request predicts this request's provider input_tokens

static_prefix_hypotheses.hypothesis: cached prefix = static head of instructions only
cached prefix = instructions only (full text, per-request tail included)
cached prefix = instructions + strict response schema

static_prefix_hypothesis_verdict: Reported, not asserted: the only locally available anchors are the two provider cached-prefix counts, and the three hypotheses cannot be separated to better than the cross-role spread shown above (instructions+schema is the most consistent on characters/unit). The dynamic evidence body is measurably denser in characters per token than the static prefix, which is why one global proxy factor mis-predicts the anchor by tens of percent. SES-001 must confirm the documented meaning of the cached prefix against the provider docs before the design relies on it.
